title: Partial availability recovery guidance & tenant requeue proofkit (draft)
content:
Purpose
This draft is a customer-facing status + post-incident guidance note targeted at tenants that observed partial availability (intermittent 5xxs and delayed streaming) during the 2029-11-25 event. It combines: (A) a concise status-page-style update for public consumption; (B) an operational checklist tenants can run to confirm recovery and safely requeue affected requests (the 'proofkit'); and (C) planned follow-ups and compensation options.

High-level summary (one-liner)
On 2029-11-25 at ~02:18 UTC Redwood experienced a partial availability incident affecting streaming and short-lived generation endpoints in eu-west and us-east regions. Most requests succeeded; a subset experienced transient failures or extended latency due to an authorization cache inconsistency during a config rollout. We mitigated the issue at 03:50 UTC and rolled a permanent fix by 2029-11-26 09:10 UTC.

Who was impacted
- Tenants using streaming endpoints and short-response generation in eu-west and us-east between 02:18–03:50 UTC.
- Observed client symptoms: 502/503 responses, truncated streams, or stalled streams followed by 504 after client-side timeout.
- Not all customers in those regions were affected; routing and per-tenant caches meant impact was uneven.

Customer-facing status page update (concise, publishable)
Title: Interim: Partial availability for streaming/generation in eu-west & us-east
Status: Resolved
Timeline: 02:18 UTC — 03:50 UTC (mitigation) / permanent fix rolled 2029-11-26 09:10 UTC
Impact: Intermittent failures and increased latency for a portion of streaming and short generation traffic. No data loss detected; some requests may have returned truncated output.
What we did: Identified a configuration cache inconsistency introduced during a rollout that caused token-authority lookups to fail intermittently on warm instances. We removed the rollout, restarted affected pools, and applied a hardening change to cache invalidation logic.
What you can do now: Verify your workloads using the attached proofkit steps (below). If you replayed requests during the window, see the 'replay guidance' section to ensure idempotency and correct ordering.
Contact: support@redwood.ai (high-touch customers: your assigned CSM will reach out).

Root cause (customer-facing summary)
During a staged configuration deployment we introduced a subtle ordering bug in how the token authority cache was warmed on recently-created worker processes. In rare timing combinations this caused in-memory authority lookups to return stale or missing entries, which then produced authorization check failures surfaced as 502/503 in the gateway. Because the runtime retries were short and streaming sessions are long-lived, some sessions were left truncated rather than fully failing, causing user-visible partial responses.

Timeline (detailed, for customers who want specifics)
- 02:18 UTC: An automated rollout of a config change began in eu-west region.
- 02:26–02:38 UTC: First alerts for elevated 5xx rates on streaming routes; SRE toggled expanded logging and began traffic sampling.
- 02:40 UTC: Remote traces showed authorization lookups returning empty for a subset of warm workers.
- 02:58 UTC: Canary rollback attempted; mixed signals due to cross-instance cache state.
- 03:12 UTC: Partial mitigation: quarantined affected worker pool and diverted traffic to nearest healthy pool (temporary routing).
- 03:50 UTC: Automated rollback fully completed; error rate returned near-normal.
- 05:00–09:10 UTC: Post-incident validation, targeted restarts, and a permanent fix for cache invalidation deployed (with staged verification).

What we verified before declaring the issue resolved
- Long-tail token verification traces matched pre-incident baseline.
- Streaming re-assembly checks showed no internal truncation remaining beyond client timeouts.
- Customer telemetry (sampled) showed successful replays returning expected outputs.

Recommended tenant actions (proofkit)
1) Quick health check (5–10 min)
   - Confirm no 502/503 spikes in your logs after 2029-11-26 09:10 UTC. Filter by request id / route if you sampled.
   - Run a small synthetic stream test from your app to the same model/route used during the incident. Check for continuous frames and end-of-stream marker.
2) Replay verification (if you retried client requests during the outage)
   - Do not automatically re-run all requests blindly. First identify idempotent vs non-idempotent operations.
   - For idempotent generation (stateless): re-run once, compare token-level delta; if outputs differ significantly, tag and escalate to support with sample ids.
   - For stateful or user-visible side effects: prefer manual reconciliation; use the per-request trace id (if present) to locate original attempt.
3) Ordering / de-duplication checks
   - If your client implements at-least-once retries, verify that your backend dedup keys were honored. If not, apply dedup keys when re-submitting.
4) If you rely on streaming partial outputs
   - Confirm your client tolerates mid-stream reconnections and can request continuation with the last-known token index.

Proofkit (concrete commands & checks)
- Synthetic stream test: curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/test-case-001
  Expected: continuous newline-delimited JSON frames for >10s, final frame containing "event":"end".
- Sample trace lookup (UI + API): paste your request-id into https://dash.redwood.internal/traces and confirm "auth_ok" events exist for the entire session.
- Replay compare: for a previously-failed request-id X, run the same prompt and capture top-3 responses; if they diverge from saved copy by >30% token-level BLEU/overlap, attach both samples to your support ticket.

Data integrity and privacy
No customer data was exfiltrated. All logs we examined were access-controlled and stored per our retention and privacy rules. We do not believe any model artifacts were corrupted.

Compensation and remediation for affected customers
- We will proactively contact tenants that had >0.1% error rate increase during the window to offer 1) a credit equivalent to the estimated excess error cost, and 2) a technical session to run the proofkit together.
- For customers who identify failed non-idempotent operations tied to the incident, we will work with you to triage on a case-by-case basis.

Planned engineering follow-ups (what we will share publicly later)
- Change slower rollout mechanics for config changes that touch the token-authority path.
- Add stronger cache-warm invariants in the runtime and a live check during rollouts.
- Improve observability surfaces so tenants can see auth-cache warming state in the dashboard.

How we'll keep you updated
- Short term: This note (publish to status page and send targeted emails to affected tenants).
- Medium term (next 2 weeks): A public post-incident report on our incident archive with an engineering write-up and code links.
- If you want an account-level technical debrief: open a high-priority ticket and request a joint session; we’ll include the SRE that led the mitigation.

Suggested short email to affected customers (template)
Subject: Update + verification steps: partial availability event (2029-11-25)
Hi <CustomerName>,
We want to inform you about a partial availability incident that may have affected some requests for streaming and short-generation routes on 2029-11-25. We have mitigated the issue and rolled a permanent fix. Please follow the attached verification checklist to confirm your traffic is clean. If you need help running the steps we’ll join a session. Apologies for the disruption — we’ve included details and next steps in the full note.
Best,
Asha (on behalf of Redwood incident response)

Open questions for review before publish
- Tone: is the phrase 'partial availability' acceptable or should we use 'intermittent failures'?
- Compensation: confirm dollar credit band for errors between 0.05%–0.5% for enterprise tenants.
- Legal review: include a short legal-approved statement about no data loss/exfiltration.

Internal notes / appendices (for internal use only; remove before public sent email)
- Affected pool ids: pool-eu-12, pool-us-07 (internal only)
- SRE runbook steps executed: quarantine -> traffic-divert -> full-rollback -> targeted restart -> permanent fix rollout.
- Key PRs: runtime cache fix PR#1284, rollout-control PR#1287.

Next steps (owner: Customer Success + SRE)
- Customer Success: identify tenant list (complete) and send targeted emails (Asha) by 2029-11-27 EOD.
- SRE: finalize post-incident report and runbook changes by 2029-12-04.
- Product/Eng: schedule rollout-safety retro and add invariant checks to CI by 2029-12-10.

End of draft

(Revision notes: initial draft 2029-10-10; added timeline detail and proofkit 2029-11-27 after engineering review)
